result:
The proposed answer of 2 is almost certainly wrong, and the argument for it is unsound.

The proposed solution says that Bombieri–Mumford classification shows the only κ=0 minimal surfaces with (p_g, q) = (1, 2) are abelian surfaces, for every prime p. That claim is not justified and does not match what I recall of the literature, which I have not re-checked here.

In characteristic 0, Chen–Hacon show that P_1 = P_2 = 1 and q = dim X imply X is birational to an abelian variety. In small positive characteristic, the argument can fail because of phenomena such as quasi-hyperelliptic surfaces and non-classical behavior in characteristics 2 and 3. As I recall, the positive-characteristic version of this characterization holds only for p > 3. If so, the smallest guaranteed prime is 5, not 2.

I did not derive this or verify the counterexamples in characteristics 2 and 3 myself, so my confidence rests on recall.

VERDICT: REJECT
